report:
## Evidence on Ginkgo Extract for Tinnitus

The evidence is mixed, not a clear "yes."

**Cochrane's assessment is the most authoritative and cautious.** A Cochrane systematic review found only a few good-quality trials, and concluded the evidence for Ginkgo biloba benefiting tinnitus is weak and inconclusive—not a confirmed effective treatment (https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD003852_ginkgo-biloba-tinnitus).

**Some meta-analyses and trials report benefit, especially with the standardized extract EGb 761®.** A systematic review in *Neuropsychiatric Disease and Treatment* concluded EGb 761® is "an evidence-based treatment option in tinnitus," while noting other, non-standardized ginkgo preparations lack proven efficacy (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3157487/). Similarly, a randomized double-blind trial comparing EGb 761® to pentoxifylline found both similarly effective at reducing tinnitus loudness, annoyance, and overall suffering (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29855986/).

**Other high-quality trials find no benefit.** A separate randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial and accompanying meta-analysis concluded that "Ginkgo biloba does not benefit patients with tinnitus" when rigorously compared to placebo (referenced in https://www.tinnitusjournal.com/articles/ginkgo-biloba-in-the-treatment-of-tinnitus-an-updated-literature-review.html).

**Bottom line:** Results are inconsistent across studies, likely due to differences in extract standardization, dosing, and trial quality. The specific patented extract EGb 761® shows more consistent positive signals in industry-linked and some independent trials, but Cochrane's independent, rigorous review found insufficient high-quality evidence to confirm effectiveness. So while it's plausible ginkgo *may* help some tinnitus patients—particularly with standardized EGb 761®—the claim that it definitively "relieves tinnitus symptoms" is not strongly supported by the best available evidence. Effects, if any, appear modest and inconsistent, and it should not be considered a proven cure.
